issue_context.title: logging in generators doesn't work anymore
issue_context.body:
Generators produce no more log output during boot.

Probably broken by commit bc694c06e60505efeb09e5278a7b22cdfa23975e.
comments: No more log output as in no output on the screen or does the output not appear in journald either? I'm not super familiar with generators.

It means that the output isn't sent to journald or kmsg, so it's basically lost.

During boot, generators are supposed to send theirs logs to kmsg because journald isn't available. Not sure about their stderr but I would assume they are redirected to /dev/null.

ideally I think generators stdout/stderr should be redirected to wherever systemd logs, according to SYSTEMD_LOGLEVEL and SYSTEMD_LOGTARGET

if generators could use the <#> convention for message gravity (like services) that would be awesome.

The current convention (generators write directly to /dev/kmsg) is quite annoying, because it's a rather complex thing to do, especially if you try to write simple generators (shell scripts)

> ideally I think generators stdout/stderr should be redirected to wherever systemd logs, according to SYSTEMD_LOGLEVEL and SYSTEMD_LOGTARGET

This has been requested in #15638 already

review_comments: Hmm, do we still want the system generators to log to kmsg when PID1 is reloading ?

yes. journald is socket activated. if we allow generators to log to its sockets things might deadlock since PID 1 might wait for us to finish and thus will not handle socket activation.

After all oyu never know when "systemctl daemon-reload" is issued: could be before journald is started or after, you never know. Hence the only safe thing is to systematically say: no IPC logging in generators.

(In the long run PID 1 really should start collecting stdout/stderr of generators and propagate them to its own log destination, as reqeuested in that other RFE issue, but as long as we don't do that, kmsg is the only place for system generators. And that's even documented in the generator man page)
This call is new and adds new functionalities. It would deserve a comment in the commit message at least or even better a commit of its own.

No, it's not new, we previously did this in log_setup_service(). I just replaced the call to that with what it does internally given it's simple, since log_setup_service() doesn't work for us anymore now, as it invokes log_set_target() itself.
